# 🎉 Congratulations! You just created your church's website repo.

You're holding a complete, mobile-first church website starter. The next 30 minutes turns this template into your church's site.

## Your next 5 steps

1. **Read the 30-minute overview** so you know what's coming → [`docs/for-tech-volunteers/01-overview.md`](../docs/for-tech-volunteers/01-overview.md)
2. **Install Node.js and Git** *(or skip this step entirely by opening the repo in GitHub Codespaces)* → [`docs/for-tech-volunteers/02-prerequisites.md`](../docs/for-tech-volunteers/02-prerequisites.md)
3. **Run `npm install` then `npm run setup`** — answers a handful of questions (church name, address, service time, color palette) and writes them in → [`docs/for-tech-volunteers/04-first-time-setup.md`](../docs/for-tech-volunteers/04-first-time-setup.md)
4. **Customize branding** — drop in your church's logo, real staff photos, and a hero image. Optionally fine-tune colors → [`docs/for-tech-volunteers/05-customize-branding.md`](../docs/for-tech-volunteers/05-customize-branding.md)
5. **Deploy to Vercel** — free hosting, live in about 2 minutes → [`docs/for-tech-volunteers/06-deploy-to-vercel.md`](../docs/for-tech-volunteers/06-deploy-to-vercel.md)

After step 5, your site is live. From there, invite your editors ([guide](../docs/for-tech-volunteers/08-grant-editor-access.md)), connect your domain ([guide](../docs/for-tech-volunteers/07-connect-domain.md)), and hand off the day-to-day to the people who'll keep it updated ([editor guide](../docs/for-editors/01-getting-started.md)).
